M_fixed: Let $g$ be smooth, $2\pi$-periodic, $\int_0^{2\pi}g=0$, $g\not\equiv0$ (model $g=\cos t$). For $u_{tt}-\Delta u=g(t)|u|^p$ on $\mathbb R^{1+3}$ with data $\varepsilon(f,h)$, $f,h\in C_c^\infty$ (solutions in the usual weak/mild sense, e.g. $C([0,T);H^1)$ with John-type weighted bounds), let $p_c(g)=\inf\{p>1:\forall f,h\ \exists\varepsilon_0>0$ such that the solution is global for all $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0\}$. Since John/Zhou/Glassey global existence uses only $|g|u|^p|\lesssim|u|^p$ and the matching Lipschitz bound, $p_c(g)\le1+\sqrt2$. Is $p_c(g)<1+\sqrt2$? Determine $p_c(g)$ and whether it depends on $g$ (a heuristic predicts 2). For $1<p<p_c(g)$, determine the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$ for suitable data.
partial_result_check: Bound p_c<=1+sqrt2 is correct: John/Zhou iteration uses only |F(u)|<=C|u|^p and |F(u)-F(v)|<=C(|u|+|v|)^{p-1}|u-v|, both hold for g(t)|u|^p. The 'resonance predicts 2' heuristic (exp of int t^{1-p}) is arithmetically right but not an argument; a normal-form attempt (H''=g) just recycles the oscillating factor, so nothing is proved. Original 'finite lifespan for p<p_c' is tautological from the inf definition, so it is replaced by a lifespan-rate question.
notes: New searches (oscillating/periodic/mean-zero coefficient, Tricomi oscillatory regime, Strauss surveys) found no prior work. Oscillatory-regime Tricomi papers concern the operator coefficient, not the source. It is a natural, decisive question that separates positivity from size. Made the solution notion explicit, put the epsilon quantifier in, and turned the redundant sub-question into a lifespan rate.

M_fixed: Let $L_n$ be uniform among Latin squares on $[n]$ and $\mathcal Q_n=([n],\circ)$ with $x\circ y=L_n(x,y)$. Prove or disprove: for every first-order sentence $\varphi$ in the language $\{\circ,=\}$, $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr[\mathcal Q_n\models\varphi]$ exists. (A 0-1 law should fail: by symbol-relabelling symmetry, $\mathbb E\#\{x:x\circ x=x\}=1$ exactly, and this count is conjecturally Poisson(1).) Expected route, as for Lynch's random unary functions: (i) w.h.p. the bounded-depth term closure of any bounded tuple is free except for coincidences counted by balanced configurations ($v$ elements, $v$ independent equations); (ii) a joint Poisson limit for the counts of all such balanced configurations, e.g. cycles of $x\mapsto x\circ x$. A disproof would need a definable sparse statistic with no limit law.
partial_result_check: There is a flaw in the first reviewer's route (i). The extension property 'every finite partial configuration extends in every consistent way w.h.p.' is false. A new x with x∘a1=b1 and x∘a2=b2 has expected count n·n^{-2}→0, because x∘a=b already determines x. The structure is functionally sparse (Lynch-type), not G(n,1/2)-type, so the route was rewritten.
notes: No prior FO-law work on Latin squares or quasigroups was found. Verified that 2509.13125 is Kwan-Petrova-Sawhney and resolves Cameron's row-parity conjecture. Even the Poisson(1) idempotent law looks unproved: the best general tool, Allsop-Morris 2606.18174, gives (δ/n)^k to (Δ/n)^k bounds, not (1+o(1))n^{-k}. So the problem is hard but well-posed.

partial_result_check: Both trivial cases check out. For alpha=2pi/k, C_alpha=R^2/Z_k: the Friedrichs modes e^{ikmθ} with Bessel order k|m| match the Z_k-invariant plane functions, and Dodson applies for any mass, with mass scaled by k. For radial data the m=0 mode on the cone is the 2D radial Laplacian. The sign convention iu_t+Δu=+|u|^2u is defocusing.
notes: Searches turned up only Ford and Blair-Ford-Marzuola Strichartz estimates, Zhang-Zheng (3D cones, H^1 small-data cubic), Gao-Wang-Xu-Zhang 2504.06045 (magnetic Strichartz on cones) and Gao-Xu 2D inverse-square (mass-supercritical). No large-L^2 mass-critical result exists on cones, AB or inverse-square 2D. 2610.29265 concerns spacetime cones and is unrelated. M is precise. This is a natural rigidity test, though somewhat incremental.
